source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A pregnancy beyond how many weeks is post-term?
questions.rationale: Post-term pregnancy exceeds 42 weeks, with risks of meconium aspiration and macrosomia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Post Term Pregnancy (PDF p. 207)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Labor lasting less than 3 hours is called:
questions.rationale: Precipitate labor lasts under 3 hours and risks lacerations and fetal intracranial hemorrhage.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Precipitate Labor (PDF p. 207)
questions.quote: Labor that lasts for less than 3 hours

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Hips flexed with knees extended and buttocks presenting is a:
questions.rationale: Frank breech: hips flexed, knees extended, buttocks present. Complete: sitting position. Footling: feet present.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Breech Delivery (PDF p. 207)
questions.quote: the hips are flexed but the knees are extended

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Meconium-stained fluid in a breech delivery is:
questions.rationale: In breech delivery, meconium staining is expected from pressure on the fetal abdomen.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Breech Delivery (PDF p. 207)
questions.quote: In Breech delivery, it is normal to see Meconium Staining

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Identical (monozygotic) twins come from:
questions.rationale: Monozygotic twins come from one ovum and one sperm and are always the same sex.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Multiple Pregnancies (PDF p. 208)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which is a complication of multiple pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Twin pregnancy raises risks of PIH, hydramnios, previa, preterm labor, anemia, and hemorrhage.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Multiple Pregnancies (PDF p. 208)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which finding defines gestational hypertension?
questions.rationale: Gestational hypertension is elevated BP without proteinuria, returning to normal after birth.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pregnancy Induced Hypertension (PDF p. 208)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: For a woman with mild pre-eclampsia, what salt intake is advised?
questions.rationale: Salt is not restricted, because restriction activates the renin-angiotensin system and raises BP.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mild Pre-eclampsia (PDF p. 209)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which assessment is essential during magnesium sulfate therapy?
questions.rationale: Check DTRs, respiratory rate, and urine output; magnesium can cause respiratory depression.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Severe Pre-eclampsia (PDF p. 209)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: What is the antidote for magnesium sulfate toxicity?
questions.rationale: Calcium gluconate is the antidote for magnesium sulfate.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Severe Pre-eclampsia (PDF p. 209)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which room environment suits a client with severe pre-eclampsia?
questions.rationale: Dim lights, limited visitors, side rails up, and suction at bedside reduce seizure risk.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Eclampsia (PDF p. 209)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: HELLP syndrome stands for:
questions.rationale: HELLP: hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets; RUQ pain from liver inflammation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, HELLP Syndrome (PDF p. 210)
questions.quote: Hemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelet (HELLP)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: When is the 50-g glucose challenge done for gestational diabetes?
questions.rationale: Screening is done at 24–28 weeks; a 1-hour value above 140 mg/dL leads to a 3-hour test.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gestational Diabetes (PDF p. 210)
questions.quote: Done at week 24 to 28 of pregnancy

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which drug is used for gestational diabetes not controlled by diet?
questions.rationale: Insulin is the therapy of choice; the handout notes oral hypoglycemics may be teratogenic.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gestational Diabetes (PDF p. 210)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A pregnant woman with heart disease has fatigue and dyspnea with ordinary activity. Which class is she?
questions.rationale: Class II: slightly compromised; ordinary activity causes fatigue, palpitations, dyspnea.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gravidocardia (PDF p. 211)
questions.quote: Ordinary physical activity causes excessive fatigue, palpitation, and dyspnea

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Decelerations mirror contractions, starting and ending with them. What causes these?
questions.rationale: Early decelerations are from head compression; late from uteroplacental insufficiency; variable from cord compression.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Variability (PDF p. 211)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Variable decelerations appear. What is the FIRST action?
questions.rationale: Variable decelerations are from cord compression; reposition (lateral or Trendelenburg); amnioinfusion may be used.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Variability (PDF p. 211)
questions.quote: Change the woman’s position from supine to lateral or trendelenburg

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: A day-1 postpartum mother wants to be cared for and talks about her birth. Which Rubin phase is this?
questions.rationale: Taking-in: passive, dependent, reviews the birth experience.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Puerperium (PDF p. 212)
questions.quote: Woman is largely passive, prefers to be taken care of

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: Lochia that is pinkish-brown on days 3 to 10 is:
questions.rationale: Rubra days 1–3 (red); serosa days 3–10 (pinkish/brown); alba day 10 to 3–6 weeks (white).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Lochia (PDF p. 212)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: Lochia changes from serosa back to rubra. What does this suggest?
questions.rationale: Lochia should never reverse; reversal suggests retained fragments. Foul odor suggests infection.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Lochia (PDF p. 212)
questions.quote: Reversal in appearance indicates retained placental fragments

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: How fast does the uterus normally involute after birth?
questions.rationale: Involution proceeds about 1 cm (one fingerbreadth) per day.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Puerperium (PDF p. 212)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: What is the most common cause of early postpartum hemorrhage?
questions.rationale: Uterine atony is most common; lacerations are second. Late hemorrhage is often from retained fragments.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Postpartum Problems (PDF p. 213)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother Following Birth
questions.stem: A non-breastfeeding mother can expect menses to return in about:
questions.rationale: Non-breastfeeding: 6–10 weeks; breastfeeding: about 6 months.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Lactation Amenorrhea (PDF p. 213)
questions.quote: If the mother is not breastfeeding, expect menstruation to return after 6 to 10 weeks
